transcript: Everyone watches women's sports, and we know that because the sirens just sold out Madison Square Garden. Now, this is the first professional women's hockey game to ever be played at the garden, and there was no way I was missing it. Truly, the vibes were the best they've ever been. Everyone was just vibrating with energy. And with the way I got there so early, cause I love to see warm UPS. And obviously, yes, I am a sirens girly, but I was extremely star struck by seeing Hillary Knight Captain America. I want her to lose tonight, but I'm always gonna cheer her on. Now, this game had a couple of the exciting things. 1 we were going to set the record for the largest women's hockey game in U S. History. Now, this record hasn't broken four times this season, but we are excited about it. 2 there are playoff implications. Sidebar. Janet Cleo sang the national anthem and I screamed. Also, Billy Jean King. Ceremonial puck drop. Anyway, sirens are currently sitting at sixth place in the league with five games left. But there's only three points separating them from Toronto, the fourth place team. And only the top four make the playoffs. So this was an important game for us. We came to play, but so did Seattle. Our goalies were both on fire. Seattle scored first, but luckily, the crowd was there to keep energy flowing. Yes, we did get some good heated rivalry. Moments, and every time the Jumbotron showed the crowd, women were kissing, and it was beautiful. And then finally, late in the third period, the sirens scored and tied it up. And then from there, kind of felt like a roller coaster. We headed into a 3 on 3 sudden death overtime, but no one scored, so we headed to the shootout. Here is my hot take. I know people hate shootouts. I love shootouts. They are intense and dramatic and stressful, and that is what I want for my hockey. Am I glad they don't exist? In the playoffs, absolutely. But for a regular game, I'm kind of always rooting for a shootout. And the sirens came through. And who want it? It was a storybook ending for a historic night. The team was emotional, the crowd was emotional, and I don't think anyone wanted to leave because it just felt so good to be there. And it's sold out Madison Square Garden supporting women's hockey, so let's keep the good vibes going. The sirens have one home game left, and let's hope this is the beginning of a beautiful friendship between women's hockey and MSG. That was so fun. I love women's hockey.
